pharm: Fluoroquinolone; inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase & topoisomerase IV; CYP1A2 inhibitor
summary: Broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone antibiotic for urinary, GI, bone/joint, skin, respiratory and other infections, and anthrax/plague. Carries a boxed warning for disabling, potentially irreversible tendon, nerve and CNS reactions; reserve for uncomplicated infections only when no alternative exists.
indications: Urinary tract infections incl. complicated UTI/pyelonephritis in children
Acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis (reserve use)
admin: May be taken with or without food
Take at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after antacids, iron, zinc, sucralfate, multivitamins, calcium or dairy
Swallow tablets whole; maintain adequate hydration to avoid crystalluria
Continue at least 2 days after symptoms resolve (except anthrax post-exposure)
moa: Bactericidal fluoroquinolone that inhibits bacterial topoisomerase II (DNA gyrase) and topoisomerase IV, enzymes required for bacterial DNA replication, transcription, repair and recombination.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to ciprofloxacin or other quinolones
relative: History of myasthenia gravis (avoid — may worsen muscle weakness)
Known QT prolongation, uncorrected hypokalemia, or QT-prolonging drugs
History of tendon disorders or prior fluoroquinolone serious reaction
monitor: Tendon pain/swelling — stop immediately if suspected
Blood glucose in diabetics on hypoglycemic agents
CNS effects and peripheral neuropathy symptoms

preg: Decades of use show no identified drug-associated risk of major birth defects or miscarriage; use if clearly needed.
lact: Excreted in human milk; consider risk to infant when prescribing during nursing.
renal: Adjust dose when CrCl <50 mL/min (q18-24h); <10% removed by dialysis.
hepatic: No routine adjustment; discontinue if signs of hepatitis (severe hepatotoxicity reported).

major: Theophylline — avoid; increased levels, CNS/seizure risk
QT-prolonging drugs (class IA/III antiarrhythmics, TCAs, macrolides, antipsychotics) — additive torsades risk
CYP1A2 substrates (e.g., tizanidine, theophylline, caffeine, clozapine) — raised levels via CYP1A2 inhibition
moderate: Oral antidiabetic agents (esp. sulfonylureas) — severe hypoglycemia, fatalities reported
Multivalent cations (antacids, iron, zinc, calcium, sucralfate, dairy, multivitamins) — reduced absorption
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; avoid dairy/calcium-fortified juice alone with the dose.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; may add to CNS effects.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive opiate urine screens (class effect).

emergency: Anaphylaxis or serious skin reaction (may occur after first dose) — seek emergency care
Sudden severe chest, back or abdominal pain (possible aortic dissection)
Tendon pain/snap/swelling — stop drug, rest limb, seek care
New numbness/tingling/weakness, seizures, or severe mood/behavior changes

monitoring: Signs of tendinitis/tendon rupture (especially >60 yrs, on steroids, transplant patients)
Renal function, hydration; LFTs if hepatic symptoms
counsel: Stop and call your doctor at first sign of tendon pain, swelling or a snap
Report numbness, tingling, weakness, mood changes or seizures immediately
Separate antacids, iron, zinc, calcium, dairy or multivitamins from your dose by several hours
Diabetics: monitor blood sugar and recognize low-sugar symptoms
Limit sun exposure and use sunscreen
Tell your doctor about sudden severe chest/back/abdominal pain
pk: Store at controlled room temperature per labeling
pearls: Boxed warning: disabling and potentially irreversible tendinitis/tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy and CNS effects can occur together — discontinue at first sign and avoid all fluoroquinolones thereafter
Reserve for acute bronchitis exacerbation, uncomplicated cystitis and sinusitis only when no other option exists
Concomitant tizanidine is contraindicated; potent CYP1A2 inhibitor that raises theophylline and caffeine levels
Avoid in myasthenia gravis — may cause life-threatening respiratory weakness
Associated with aortic aneurysm/dissection, especially in elderly and those with vascular risk factors
Tendon rupture risk rises with age >60, corticosteroids and organ transplant
Separate from multivalent cations (antacids, iron, calcium, dairy) to preserve absorption
missed: Take as soon as remembered; skip if near the next dose. Do not double up.
overdose: Empty stomach, maintain hydration, supportive care, monitor renal function and urine pH (reversible renal toxicity reported); <10% removed by dialysis.
refs: U.S. FDA label via openFDA / DailyMed
